points.note: Only cylinder-gear roller visible from this angle (uniform-diameter knurled cylinder, not tapered, matching ch13 reference). Placed on the bright axle/bearing pin visible through the black mounting bracket at the gear's front end face, which is the true rotation-axis point rather than an estimate from the partly-occluded disc rim.

Narrow tip end of the single most face-on rocker arm (frontmost blade in the ~20-arm fan, matching the arm etched 'rocker arm' in the ch14 reference). The blade converges to a genuinely sharp point here, so tip_left and tip_right are only ~3px apart.
See tip_left note - same tip vertex, opposite edge of the blade's thickness.

Wide/pivot end of the same arm, at its upper edge just before the vertical support rod crosses it. Genuine ambiguity here: near the pivot, this arm's material visually merges with a pivot hinge bracket and possibly with the butts of neighboring arms in the fan, so the exact corner vertex is partly occluded by the rod and the hinge casting.
Lower edge counterpart of butt_left, placed near the visible pivot bolt. Same occlusion caveat as butt_left applies.
Left terminal end of the top green frame casting (rounded boss around the corner support rod).
Near corner of the top frame where the back face meets the right face; a rod collar/boss sits right at the vertex so the precise corner point is estimated from the surrounding casting edges.
Right terminal end of the top frame casting.
Left corner of the green base slab, clearly visible kink in the bottom edge.
Near corner of the base where the back face meets the right face, visible as a clear diagonal-to-highlight transition next to the corner support rod.
Right corner of the green base slab, rounded terminal edge clearly visible.

occluded.reason: The pinion sprocket and the large brass crank-drive gear sit at platen level on the machine's FRONT face (confirmed by cross-referencing the front view page002_img01.png, which shows this gear pair directly below the paper platen). This back-right three-quarter view shows no paper/platen at all, confirming the front face is fully turned away from the camera; the assembly is hidden by the machine's own frame.

The crank and its axle sprocket (ch11 reference) are mounted at the base on the machine's front-facing side; not visible from this back-right angle - occluded by the black base slab and the green corner post.

A second cylinder-gear roller would sit alongside/behind the visible one (per ch13 reference, cylinder gears are a meshing pair), but it is fully hidden behind the green pyramidal post and black base slab in this view.
The conical gear stack (ch12 reference) is mounted at the base but is entirely hidden behind the green pyramidal post and black base slab from this back-right angle; no portion of it is visible.
Far-side corner of the top frame, on the machine's front face; not visible from this back-right three-quarter angle.
Far-side corner of the base slab, on the machine's front face; not visible from this back-right three-quarter angle.

orientation_note: Back-right three-quarter view: the camera sees the machine's BACK face (wide, spanning the left portion of the frame) and the RIGHT side face (narrower, right portion), meeting at a near corner around x=827-854. The FRONT/platen face (paper holder, pinion/crank drive gear) is fully turned away and not visible anywhere in this image.
